title: Thankful for Fellowship
body:
I am thankful for "fellowship in the gospel" among my brothers and sisters in Christ! Paul addresses this idea in the opening lines of his letter to the Philippian church.

The Book of Philipians is a "prison epistle", because Paul wrote it during one of the many times he was suffering in a prison for his faith.

The Book of Philippians is also known as "the epistle of joy" because of his frequency of using the words "joy" and "rejoice": 16 times amongst only 104 verses. That's an average of once in every 6 1/2 verses.

Philippians 1:1-5

"servants" (v1) = denotes a willing slave who is happily and loyally linked to his master (That is what we all should be if we are a Christian - humble obedience.)

"saints" (v1) = fellow believers united with the death, burial, and resurrection of Jesus Christ. (That is what we all are if we are a Christian.)

Verses 3-5 makes me think of 3 things we can be thankful for.

Thankful for Memories (v3)

Thankful for Prayer (v4)

Thankful for Fellowship (v5)

We Can Be Thankful For Memories

"I thank my God upon every remembrance of you" (v3)

We all have good memories and bad memories

EVERY remembrance would have to include some bad times during the birth of this Philippian church he is writing to. Surely Paul could remember when the multitude rose up against them, beat them, whipped them, and cast them into prison! (Acts 16:22-23) Not the type of things we would normally thank God for!

We have to focus on the positive aspects of EVERY remembrance.

"...and bringing into captivity every thought to the obedience of Christ." (2 Corinthians 10:5)

Instead of dwelling on those hurtful and painful memories Paul could focus on how God sent a great earthquake to open the prison doors and how their Phillipian jailer asked "what must I do to be saved?" (saved = same word translated "whole" when Jesus told the leper "Thy faith hath made thee whole" in Luke 17:19)

Paul could remember how God led him to answer the jailer, "Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house." He could remember that the jailer "rejoiced believing in God with all his house." Paul could focus on his remembrance that they were all saved and baptized! (Acts 16:25-34)

Even though hurtful and painful memories existed, he could focus on the positive aspects and say "I thank my God upon every remembrance of you."

We Can Be Thankful for Prayer

We can talk to God at any time!

"Always in every prayer of mine" (v4)

Jesus gave us the example

Praying early in the morning. (Mark 1:35)

Praying all night. (Luke 6:12)

(Mark 6:46, Luke 5:16, Luke 9:18, Luke 22:41, & others)

"Praying always with all prayer and supplication in the Spirit, and watching thereunto with all perseverance and supplication for all saints;" (Ephesians 6:18)

We can pray for everyone!

"for you all" (v4)

intercessory prayer is praying for the needs of others

"I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men;"

-(1 Timothy 2:1)

Prayer should be a joy, not a job!

"making request with joy" (v4)

"...in thy presence is fullness of joy..." (Psalm 16:11)

"My meditation of him (God) shall be sweet: I will be glad in the LORD." (Psalm 104:34)

We Can Be Thankful For Fellowship

"For your fellowship in the gospel..." (v5)

fellowship = a commercial term for a joint-partnership in a business venture in which all parties actively participate to ensure the success of the business.

fellowship = In the Christian community the word expresses intimacy with Christ and other believers.

fellowship = 2 fellows in 1 ship ~ The Gospel Ship!

"And they continued steadfastly in the apostles doctrine, and fellowship, and in the breaking of bread, and in prayers."

-(Acts 2:42)

Believers need fellowship with one another!

"And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and good works: Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more as ye see the day approaching." (Hebrews 10:24)

"Wherefore comfort yourselves together, and edify one another..." (1 Thessalonians 5:11)

3 words we don't use much anymore, as defined in Websters dictionary in 1828:

  • provoke = To call into action; to arouse, to excite.

  • exhort = To encourage, to embolden, to cheer, to advise. The primary sense seems to be to excite or to give strength, spirit, or courage.

  • edify = To instruct and improve the mind in knowledge generally, and particularly in moral and religious knowledge, in faith and holiness.

Fellowship enables us to provoke, exhort, and edify one another!

Fellowship is possible because of God!

"But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin." (1 John 1:7)

Not everyone has this sweet fellowship Paul wrote about because some do not truly have any fellowship with God to start with.

Are you in fellowship with God?

"If we say that we have fellowship with him, and walk in darkness, we lie, and do not the truth." (1 John 1:6)

If you are not in fellowship with God, why not? Jesus is waiting!

Think about Jesus standing outside the door to your heart, wanting you to let him in so he can forgive you and save you!

"Behold, I stand at the door, and knock: if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come into him, and will sup with him, and he with me." (Revelation 3:20)

"Sup" means to enjoy fellowship with Him!

3 Things We Can (and Should) Be Thankful For:

  • Thankful for Every Remembrance (v3)

  • Thankful for Prayer (v4)

  • Thankful for Fellowship (v5)

I pray all of you have a wonderful and blessed Thanksgiving Holiday!

title: Are you Truly Thankful?
body:
The cleansing of the 10 lepers in Luke 17:11-19 causes me to reflect on whether I am TRULY THANKFUL, as I ought to be.

Glorifying God and giving thanks to Jesus (v15-16)

Is always expected (v17)

But seldom expressed (v18)

Luke records some of Jesus teaching just prior to the 10 lepers meeting him in Luke 17:3-10. I'm reminded of 3 elements that give us the ability to be TRULY THANKFUL:

  • FORGIVENESS

  • FAITH

  • OBEDIENCE

FORGIVENESS (v3-4)

It's not about keeping score, it's about losing count!

  • It's difficult to be thankful when you are keeping score.

  • It's difficult to be thankful when you are holding grudges.

"Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour, and evil speaking, be put away from you, with all malice: And be ye kind one to another, tender hearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ's sake hath forgiven you." (Ephesians 4:31-32)

I am glad Jesus did not keep score.

"Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do." (Luke 23:34)

He wants us to receive His forgiveness!

"If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness."

(1 John 1:9)

We won't be TRULY THANKFUL until we experience complete FORGIVENESS by God, and are able to forgive others!

FAITH (v5-6)

It's not about the size of faith, it's about the Source of faith!

A mustard seed is very small.

A small amount of faith in a Great Saviour is what we need!

  • Salvation!

  • Peace with God!

"For by grace are ye saved, through faith..." (Ephesians 2:8)

"Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ." (Romans 5:1)

We won't be TRULY THANKFUL until we have exercised SAVING FAITH in Jesus Christ!

OBEDIENCE (v 7-10)

It's not about deserving something, it's about duty to Someone!

  • We should not be obedient just to get a reward.

  • The Pharisees thought they deserved something from God because of their good works. (We do, too, sometimes.)

Salvation is "...not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast." (Ephesians 2:8-9)

We are obedient to God and serve Him and one another because He loves us and we love Him.

We were made for this!

  • "For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them." (Ephesians 2:10)

  • "Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: fear God and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man" (Ecclesiastes 12:13)

Our attitude should be one of humility.

"...we have done that which was our duty to do." (Luke 17:10)

We won't be TRULY THANKFUL until we are enjoying a life of humble OBEDIENCE to God.

After teaching about FORGIVENESS, FAITH, and OBEDIENCE: (v3-10)

"there met him ten men" (V12)

They had the same need of FORGIVENESS

They had the same initial OBEDIENCE

They did NOT have the same saving FAITH

All had the same condition:

they "were lepers" (v12)

they "stood afar off" (v12)

Leprosy was a picture of sin: ugly, wretched, miserable, defiling the whole body, separating, alienating, making outcasts, no hope for cure and leading to death.

We can identify with their condition, spiritually.

"All have sinned and come short of the glory of God" (Romans 3:23)

All 10 had the same request:

"Jesus, Master, have mercy on us." (v13)

All 10 men were sinners needing FORGIVENESS.

These 10 men had the same initial OBEDIENCE.

"Go show yourselves unto the priests. And it came to pass, that, as THEY WENT..."

Jesus told them what to do and they did it.

But when it came to FAITH :

  • Only 1 had a Saving Faith

  • 9 had a Shallow Faith

The same word translated as "whole" in verse 19 is also translated as "saved" in many other verses. (Matthew 1:21, Matthew 18:11, Luke 9:56, Luke 19:10, Acts 2:21, Acts 4:12, Acts 16:31, Romans 10:9, Romans 10:13, & many others.)

The Saving FAITH of the 1 moved him to True Thanksgiving!

He glorified God (v15)

He worshiped Jesus (v16)

He was made whole (v19)

The source of his faith was Jesus Christ!

The Shallow FAITH of the 9 moved them to ... what?

"Where are the 9?" (v17)

They are "not found" (v18)

The source of their faith was... what?

Only one was "found" healthy AND whole that day.

Physically healed and Spiritually whole.

Nine were found healthy but NOT whole that day.

Healed of leprosy, but still had a sin problem.

To be TRULY THANKFUL this Thanksgiving we need to:

  • Experience complete FORGIVENESS by God!

  • Exercise saving FAITH in Jesus Christ!

  • Enjoy a life of humble OBEDIENCE to The Lord!

I pray everyone will have a happy and blessed Thanksgiving holiday, and that you will be TRULY THANKFUL!

title: The Testimony of The LORD Is Sure!
body:
"...the testimony of the LORD is sure, making wise the simple." (Psalm 19:7b)

The More Sure Word

(2 Peter 1:16-21)

  • Powerful (v16-18)

  • Preserved (v19)

  • Practical (v19)

The Powerful Word

  • Not "cunningly devised fables" (2 Peter 1:16)

  • "The word of God is quick and powerful..." (Hebrews 4:12)

  • "...converting the soul." (Psalm 19:7)

Testimony of the LORD = The divine witness

"This is my beloved son, in whom I am well pleased"

(2 Peter 1:17)

The Preserved Word

  • "We have also a more sure word..." (2 Peter 1:19)

  • "The words of the LORD are pure words; as silver tried in a furnace of earth, purified seven times. Thou shalt keep them O LORD, thou shalt preserve them from this generation forever." (Psalm 12:6-7)

  • "The grass witherest, the flower fadeth; but the word of our God shall stand for ever." (Isaiah 40:8)

  • "Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away." (Matthew 24:35)

The Practical Word

  • "All things that pertain unto life and godliness" (2 Peter 1:3)

  • "making wise the simple" (Psalm 19:7)

  • "ye do well that ye take heed, as unto a light that shineth in a dark place" (2nd Peter 1:19)

  • "...This is my beloved son, in whom I am well pleased. Hear ye him" (Matthew 17:5)

title: What Good Is God's Law?
body:
"The law of the LORD is perfect, converting the soul" (Psalm 19:7a)

"Law of the LORD"

  • Divine teaching from God to man

"perfect"

  • Without flaw or defect; inerrant

  • Complete; all that is needed

"converting the soul"

  • Exposes the sin which destroys

  • Expounds the Saviour Who delivers!

"I had not known sin, but by the law: for I had not known lust except the law had said thou shalt not covet" (Romans 7:7)

"Wherefore the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ, that we might be justified by faith." (Galatians 3:24)

title: Some Great Words About A Great Book!
body:
THE BIBLE contains the mind of God, the state of man, the way of salvation, the doom of sinners, and the happiness of believers. Its doctrines are holy, its precepts are binding, its histories are true, and its decisions are immutable.

Read it to be wise, believe it to be safe, and practice it to be holy. It contains light to direct you, food to support you, and comfort to cheer you.

It is the traveler’s map, the pilgrim’s staff, the pilot’s compass, the soldier’s sword, and the Christian’s charter. Here Paradise is restored, Heaven opened, and the gates of hell disclosed.​

CHRIST is its grand subject, our good the design, and the glory of God its end. It should fill the memory, rule the heart, and guide the feet. Read it slowly, frequently, and prayerfully. It is a mine of wealth, a paradise of glory, and river of pleasure.

It is given you in life, will be opened at the judgment, and be remembered forever. It involves the highest responsibility, will reward the greatest labor, and will condemn all who trifle with its sacred contents.

- From the preface in a Gideon's New Testament.

title: Do You Have Enemies?
body:
As Christians, we have enemies, both physical and spiritual. Even when things are going well for us, and we are experiencing the mighty blessings of God, Satan is there, somewhere in the background, walking about "seeking whom he may devour". (1 Peter 5:8)

Sometimes he uses people. "For many walk, of whom I have told you often, and now tell you even weeping, that they are the enemies of the cross of Christ". (Philippians 3:18)

Psalm 58 is one of many imprecatory Psalms, and reminds us we can, and should, deal with the enemy. Even in the good times.

Psalm 58:1-11

Prepare for the Enemy (v1-5)

Expect the enemy to be:

Unrighteous and Unjust (v1)

Heartless and Violent (v2)

Wicked from the womb (v3)

Speaking lies (v3)

Poisonous, dangerous, and out of control (v4-5)

Pray Against the Enemy (v6-8)

Pray their Power will be Disabled (v6)

Pray their Plans will be Disappointed (v7)

Pray their Purpose will be Destroyed (v8)

Perceive the Ultimate Destruction of the Enemy (v9-11)

Their destruction comes quickly and surely. (v9)

Their destruction comes with God's wrath. (v9)

Their destruction comes with God's vengeance. (v10)

Their destruction comes with God's righteous judgement. (v11)

How to destroy an enemy:
"Therefore if thine enemy hunger, feed him; if he thirst, give him drink: for in so doing thou shalt heap coals of fire on his head. Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good." (Romans 12:20-21)

If you are living as an enemy of God, God's people desire you to be saved from the wrath and judgement that is sure to come.

That is also God's desire for you!

"Much more then, being now justified by his (Jesus) blood, we shall be saved from wrath through him. For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life." (Romans 5:9-10)

title: Are You an Enemy of God?
body:
In the midst of writing about his rejoicing and joy concerning the type of church the Thessalonians had become, the Apostle Paul turned his thoughts to the enemies of the church in 1 Thessalonians 2:15-16.

#1. They Fight the Power of God (v15)

They killed the Lord Jesus

They killed the prophets

They persecuted the apostles

Stephen spoke to them this way in Acts 7:51-52: "Ye stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, ye do always resist the Holy Ghost: as your fathers did, so do ye. Which of the prophets have not your fathers persecuted? and they have slain them which shewed before of the coming of the Just One; of whom you have been now the betrayers and murderers:" Six verses later they stoned him to death.

Lost people today are not just fighting the people of God, but they are fighting the very Power of God those people represent! Power that is mighty to save!

Are you fighting God's power? "ye do always resist the Holy Ghost"

#2. They Forbid the Word of God (v16a)

"that they might be saved"

"But these are written, that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye might have life through his name." (John 20:31)

Most lost folks today are not forbidding the Word of God from being preached, but they all ARE forbidding the Word of God from taking root in their heart so that they might be saved.

Are you forbidding God's Word to have its effectual work in your life?

#3. They Fill Up Their Sin Against God (v16b)

"to fill up their sins alway"

As Jesus spoke to the Jews, "Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do..." (John 8:44)

In Genesis 15:16 God noted to Abraham that "the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full". But eventually their iniquity (sin) caught up with them.
God is "not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance." (2 Peter 3:9)

“If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.” (1 John 1:9)

Are you filling up your sin against God?

#4 They Face the Wrath of God (v16c)

"for the wrath is come upon them to the uttermost"

In Ephesians 5 Paul gives a long list of common sins that people try to get away with. Then he writes in verse 6 "Let no man deceive you with vain words: for because of these things cometh the wrath of God upon the children of disobedience."

Are you facing the wrath of God?

You don't have to face God's wrath. You can be saved and forgiven! It all comes down to faith and belief.

"He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life: and he that believeth not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God abideth on him." (John 3:36)

None of us should be God's enemy!

Please, DO NOT:

Fight the Power of God

Forbid the Word of God

Fill Up Sin Against God

Face the Wrath of God

title: Be A Paul!
body:
The example of Apostle Paul's life is one we should all follow, as he wrote "Be ye followers of me, even as I also am of Christ." (1 Corinthians 11:1)

And I desire to pattern my ministry after that of Paul. We have his example of ministry all over the New Testament, and a few of his characteristics stand out in 1 Thessalonians 2:1-12.

He Was Confident In God's Power (v1-2)

Amidst suffering (v2a)

Amidst shame (v2b)

Amidst contention (v2c)

He Was Centered On God's Truth (v3-5)

Not on mischief (v3)

Not on man-pleasing (v4-5)

Not on money (v5)

He Was Committed To God's Love (v6-11)

He exhibited the humble love of God (v6)

He exhibited the nurturing love of God (v7)

He exhibited the sacrificial love of God (v8-9)

He exhibited the righteous love of God (v10)

He exhibited the authoritative love of God (v11)

All because he wanted folks to be saved and able to have a life "worthy of God who hath called you unto his kingdom and glory."! (v12)

title: My Kind Of Church!
body:
The church of the Thessalonians was my kind of church!

In 1 Thessalonians chapter 1 Paul recognized what kind of church they were:

They Were A Sincere Church! (1:1-3)

  • Work of faith (v3)

  • Labor of love (v3)

  • Patience of hope (v3)

They Were A Surrendered Church! (1:4-6)

  • They were chosen (v4)

  • They received the word (v6)

  • They repented (v9)

  • They followed the Lord (v6)

(They surrendered themselves to be like Christ!)

They Were A Sounding Out Church! (1:7-9)

  • Their LIVES sounded out and pointed people to Christ (v7)

  • Their WORDS sounded out and pointed people to Christ (v8)

"ensample" = pattern

"sounded out" = echo

They sounded out Christ (v8)

to the north (Macedonia)

to the south (Achaia)

"also in every place" (wherever they went!)

They Were A Second Coming Church! (v10)

  • They were looking for Christ's return!

Jesus said "...I go to prepare a place for you. And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again, and receive you unto myself, that where I am, there ye may be also." (John 14:2,3)

The Church of the Thessalonians knew that people needed to come to Jesus now, because Jesus would be coming back soon!

"And the Spirit and the bride say, Come. And let him that is athirst come. And whosoever will, let him take the water of life freely." (Revelation 22:17)

"He which testifieth these things saith, Surely I come quickly. Amen. Even so come, Lord Jesus." (Rev 22:20)

A footnote about Flat Gap Baptist Church:

I am very grateful I get to serve in a church that is similar to that one at Thessalonica! There's always room for improvement, but WOW, what a church we have at Flat Gap Baptist!

A Sincere Church!

A Surrendered Church!

A Sounding Out Church!

A Second Coming Church!

photo.alt: My Kind Of Church!, Flat Gap Baptist Church

title: Do You Stumble In Serving God?
body:
My #1 stumbling block that hinders me from doing what God wants is... me! I feel I'm not good enough, or I don't know enough. I'm just not sure enough, or think I can't do enough to be successful for God.

But then I'm reminded of 1 Corinthians 1:26-29.

"For you see your calling, brethern, how that not many wise men after the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble are called: But God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty; And base things of the world, and things which are despised, hath God chosen, yea, and things which are not, to bring to nought things that are: That no flesh should glory in his presence."

And verse 31 "That according as it is written, He that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord."

In Exodus 3 and 4 we learn how God used Moses, even though Moses felt the same stumbling blocks I do. God answers our every stumbling block!

Stumbling Block #1: Lack of Self Esteem.

"Who am I?" (Exodus 3:11)

We should glory that God is with us! (Ex. 3:12)

Stumbling Block #2: Lack of Knowledge

Moses didn't know God's name. (Ex. 3:13)

We should glory that we know God, The Great I AM! (Ex. 3:14 & Jeremiah 9:23-24)

Stumbling Block #3: Lack of Confidence

"They will not believe me, nor hearken unto my voice." (Ex. 4:1)

We should glory that God uses what we have!

"What is that in thine hand?" (Ex. 4:2)

Stumbling Block #4: Lack of Ability

"I am not eloquent...I am slow of speech, and of a slow tongue." (Ex. 4:10)

We should glory in God's grace! (Ex. 4:11 & 2 Corinthians 12:9-10)

Moses succeeded and so will we! Not because of our own wisdom, or might, or riches, or of anything of ourselves. It's all God!

"That according as it is written, He that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord."

title: Not Just A Fish Story
body:
There are some lessons to gain from the account of Peter with Jesus at Lake Gennesart in Luke 5:1-11:

I want to be faithful to God...

...when asked to do little things (v3)

...when it does not make sense (v4-5)

...when I need help (v6-7)

...when I feel unworthy (v8)

...when I'm astonished and afraid (v9-10)

...when Jesus calls! (v10-11)

Luke 5:1-11

title: Do You Want To Triumph?
body:
In 2 Corinthians 2:11-17 we see that there is Victory in Jesus even in the midst of despair and depression. Paul had "no rest in my spirit" in verse 13 and actually went away from "a door opened unto me of the Lord". But then his attention turned to Jesus!

Even when we don't feel great, God reminds us of the following truths:

We are Triumphant Winners in Christ! (v14)

We are Triumphant Witnesses for Christ! (v15-16)

We Share the Triumphant Words of Christ! (v17)

"Now thanks be unto God which always causeth us to triumph in Christ and maketh manifest the savour of his knowledge by us in every place" -2 Corinthians 2:14
